commands.review_summary:
The branch changes Worker Hetzner provisioning and fleet cleanup to roll back or persist failed server and SSH-key cleanup IDs, adds LeaseRecord cleanup fields, and expands Worker regression tests.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection of current main shows a Hetzner readiness failure can occur after server creation while the failed lease lacks cleanup-addressable cloudID/serverID; I did not run a live Hetzner allocation in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Human follow-up is needed because automation cannot supply the contributor's live Hetzner account proof; the remaining code cleanup is the changelog removal.

target.title: fix(worker): roll back partial Hetzner provisioning
target.body:
## Summary

- roll back a Hetzner server when post-create readiness fails, treating already-absent resources as successfully cleaned up
- continue through retryable server-type fallbacks after a successful rollback
- delete only newly created canonical lease-owned SSH keys; retain shared workspace, reused, and custom keys
- persist exact key cleanup work when immediate deletion fails, retry it with coordinator backoff, and finish it before workspace reprovisioning
- persist the exact server and key IDs when rollback deletion fails, defer cleanup without hot-looping, and retry server-before-key so an attached key is never removed first
- honor an explicit no-delete release by retaining pending exact server/key cleanup without alarms, while preserving a later explicit delete path

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/761

## Verification

Current exact head: `538e36842d4f5c05f2e4fb53235e01f8d863b1cf` (merged current `main` without rewriting contributor history). Exact-head CI is running.

- `npm test --prefix worker` — 765 tests passed before the current-main merge
- `npm test --prefix worker -- fleet.test.ts` — 356 tests passed after the current-main merge
- `npm test --prefix worker -- azure.test.ts` — 37 tests passed after the current-main merge
- `npm run format:check --prefix worker`
- `npm run lint --prefix worker`
- `npm run check --prefix worker`
- `npm run build --prefix worker`
- `scripts/check-docs.sh` — 51 command docs, 69 providers, 202 Markdown files, and the generated docs site
- autoreview found and drove a retained-workspace alarm-loop fix; the second review reported no actionable findings

No new live Hetzner canary was run because the saved token does not authenticate. The regression suite exercises successful rollback, server and key 404 idempotency, fallback continuation, durable server/key ID recovery after rollback failure, server-before-key cleanup, exact-ID persistence/retry, retry backoff and early-alarm suppression, shared/reused-key retention, explicit no-delete retention for server+key and key-only states, workspace alarm quiescence, and later explicit deletion.
